script.flip1: BUF's 33% blitz gets home the way Stafford's sample says it does (EPA -0.33 on 44 blitzed dropbacks vs +0.19 unblitzed). Deep Adams yards stall, checkdowns to Kyren and Higbee spike, and if BUF leads late LA's rush volume dies with the clock.

Or BUF falls behind LA's 3.96 YPC run defense, Cook's 6.4 YPC regresses toward that rate, and Allen has to throw into the tightest part of LA's defense.

The overlap that survives that flip is Kyren (22 targets, 95 air yards, 6.8 yards/target) and Higbee (17 targets, 142 air yards) into a 33% blitz and an 8.13 middle YPA. Cook's 57 carries and 6.4 YPC run into LA's best unit; 19 carries at 3.96 YPC is about 75 yards, on top of the 76.5 rush line, so he is not an overlap over.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because the blitz story never showed up on the field. BUF sat in a shell the pack does not chart, Stafford's -0.33 blitz EPA never got a chance to matter, and LA stayed on schedule with Corum mixing 7.7 carries a game so Kyren's passing-down targets collapsed from 7.3 to a couple of swings under 22 yards. Higbee lost the tight-end checks to Ferguson, who already had 11 targets and 63 yards in the same three-game window, and finished 1 for 9. A late inactive the pack does not list would zero either leg the same way. That counter is real on role concentration and missing charting, but it is not stronger than a 22-target and 17-target base against lines of 22.5 and 25.5, so the legs stay flagged rather than cut.
slip_story: One story only: BUF pressure and a middle that allows 8.13 YPA funnel LA toward short RB and TE targets. Stack Kyren recyds over 22.5 with Higbee recyds over 25.5. Do not add Adams over 62.5 or Coleman over 39.5, which need clean deep shots, the opposite of the blitz flip. Do not add Cook rush over 76.5, which needs efficiency LA's 3.96 YPC allowed does not support. No TDs, no receptions, one market per player.
